/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 2

*References:*
- [E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research
  with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture2

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

open scoped Classical in
/--
WOWII [Conjecture 2](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$Ls(G) \ge 2 \cdot (l(G) - 1)$ where $l(G)$ is the average independence number of
the neighbourhoods of the vertices of $G$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763), where an informal proof is also provided.

Another formal proof combines a spanning-tree leaf bound from connected domination
with an ordered-pair double-counting argument for adjacent neighbourhoods.

A third formal proof starts from a triangle-free spanning subgraph of $G$ with the maximum
number of edges. Maximality bounds the neighbourhood independence number of each vertex by its
degree in that subgraph; an edge whose endpoint degrees sum to at least $2 \cdot l(G)$ then
carries a double star, which is acyclic and extends to a spanning tree with at least
$2 \cdot (l(G) - 1)$ leaves.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphaproof-nexus-results/blob/0647711a71183c1ea492ad60860776617ce1ea88/APNOutputs/AICollaborator/Graphs/GraphConjecture2.lean#L704",
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/kingcharlezz/formal-conjectures/blob/7d88e8b7946791ff53c322651f73de8d4df0ba53/FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/Proofs/GraphConjecture2.lean#L622",
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/wowii-graph-conjecture-2-lean/blob/fc6cc1f5b857e9c3f9693b98587660eb09606abc/lean/GraphConjecture2.lean#L673"]
theorem conjecture2 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
  2 * (averageIndepNeighbors G - 1) ≤ Ls G := by sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture2

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement assumes `[Nontrivial α]` (at least 2 vertices). The source states the conjecture for every simple connected finite graph, which includes the one-vertex graph K₁.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a subsingleton vertex type, every neighbourhood is empty (graphs are loopless). So each `indepNeighborsCard` is 0 and `averageIndepNeighbors G = 0`. `Ls G` is an sSup of naturals cast to ℝ, so it is ≥ 0 (`Real.sSup_nonneg`). The inequality becomes −2 ≤ Ls G, which is trivially true. The hypothesis therefore only removes a case where the claim holds anyway. The independent formal proof by KitaKen1 proves the statement without `Nontrivial` by treating the subsingleton case separately.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. The theorem states exactly the WOWII Conjecture 2 claim: for every simple, connected, finite graph G, L(G) ≥ 2(avg_v μ(v) − 1). Here μ(v) = α(G[N(v)]) and L(G) is the maximum number of leaves of a spanning tree.

Source access: the WOWII page (cms.dt.uh.edu) could not be reached. Port 443 timed out, including through a reader proxy, and archive.org and archive.ph were unavailable. The wording therefore comes from DeLaVina (the list's author) and Waller, EJC 2008. They quote it as "Conjecture 4 (Graffiti [13], conjecture 2). Let G be a graph. Then L ≥ 2(average of μ(v) − 1)", with [13] = Written on the Wall II. The arXiv 2605.22763 source states the same theorem.

The arXiv main text (line ~133) loosely says "the maximum number, over all vertices v, of independent sets in the neighbourhood of v". This is a sloppy paraphrase. Its own appendix theorem uses the average, and a max version would be false: for K₁,₃, max local independence is 3, so 2(3−1) = 4, but a 4-vertex tree has at most 3 leaves. The Lean correctly uses the average.

Definition checks in Lean (scratch files only):
- `decide` confirms the local independence numbers of C₄ (all 2) and K₁,₃ (3 at the centre, 1 at the leaves).
- I proved `averageIndepNeighbors (cycleGraph 4) = 2`, `Ls (cycleGraph 4) ≤ 2`, and `2 ≤ Ls G` for every connected G on ≥ 2 vertices. So Ls(C₄) = 2 and the Lean inequality is tight at C₄, exactly as the source's is. Neither definition is inflated or deflated.
- `Ls` is an sSup over a finite, non-empty, bounded set when G is connected, so it equals the maximum. Its value of 0 for disconnected graphs cannot be reached here.

Status: `research solved` is correct. EJC 2008 listed the conjecture as open; the arXiv 2026 paper reports it proved.

formal_proof links:
- The APN file at the pinned commit has `theorem conjecture2 ... : 2 * (l G - 1) ≤ Ls G` at L704, where `l` is an abbrev for `averageIndepNeighbors`. It has no sorry or axioms.
- The KitaKen1 theorem at L673 proves the statement without `Nontrivial`. After two one-line Mathlib-API-drift patches (`G.loopless.irrefl`, and a `spanningCoe = T` rewrite), I compiled it against this repository's own definitions. `#print axioms` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, and it proves the repository's exact statement.

The proof sketches in the docstring are mathematically sound (I checked the triangle-free maximal subgraph argument by hand). They are not a statement defect.
